contract.note: Generated from the backend, consumed by the console as a typed client. Frozen in W1 before parallel work starts. The only synchronisation point between the two tracks.

App Volumes Agent as a managed prerequisite

decisions.decision: NHibernate with FluentNHibernate for data access
decisions.rationale: Explicit mapping control; consistent with other projects in this estate

decisions.decision: Versioned migrations via FluentMigrator, not NHibernate SchemaUpdate
decisions.rationale: Community users will upgrade between releases and must keep their data

decisions.decision: SQLite stores metadata only; binaries live on an artifact volume, referenced by path plus SHA-256
decisions.rationale: Multi-hundred-megabyte blobs in SQLite would wreck both the database and backups

decisions.decision: SQLite in WAL mode with writes serialised in the backend
decisions.rationale: Prevents SQLITE_BUSY under concurrent multi-tenant fan-out; must be designed in from the start

decisions.decision: Kestrel serves the Angular static build and terminates TLS; no separate reverse proxy
decisions.rationale: HAProxy cannot serve static files, so it would add a layer rather than replace one. One container and one config language lowers the barrier for contributors

decisions.decision: Docker Compose is the unit of deployment; the agent stays outside Docker as a Windows service
decisions.rationale: Backend stays portable and stateless; MSI work has to happen on Windows

decisions.decision: Agents authenticate with mTLS client certificates, private key in the Windows certificate store
decisions.rationale: The agent can execute commands on the station and publish to production tenants, making it the most valuable component to compromise. Revocation is server-side

decisions.decision: MQTT carries notifications, progress and heartbeat/LWT; HTTPS carries job state and artifacts; a polling fallback is mandatory
decisions.rationale: MQTT gives NAT-friendly push and free offline detection, but is not a durable job queue and cannot move large files. The broker must not become a single point of failure

decisions.decision: A JSON package manifest is the user-facing interface to automation; templates compose by inheritance
decisions.rationale: Engineers describe intent instead of digging into the build engine; imperative steps remain as an escape hatch

decisions.decision: Workspace ONE Freestyle Orchestrator is the deployment engine; the console generates workflow JSON and does not build a competing DSL
decisions.rationale: Install order, conditions and branching already execute natively in the platform. Removes an entire orchestration engine from scope

decisions.decision: App Volumes Agent is a separate managed prerequisite package enforced as the first conditional Freestyle step (variant A), not chained into every MSI (variant B)
decisions.rationale: Variant B would duplicate a platform capability and produce N copies of the agent, with version conflicts and painful upgrades

decisions.decision: Manifests reference logical names; a resolver maps them to tenant-local IDs at publish time, and republishing updates the existing workflow idempotently
decisions.rationale: Freestyle identifiers are tenant-local, so one workflow file cannot be copied across tenants. This is the core value of the product

decisions.decision: Work split - Codex owns frontend, Cloud owns backend, agent, integrations and CI; OpenAPI is the contract
decisions.rationale: Enables parallel work with a single synchronisation point

decisions.decision: MVP is narrow: MSI plus Windows internal apps plus multi-tenant publish. MSIX, macOS and capture automation deferred to v0.2
decisions.rationale: Four weeks to deadline; scope discipline is the only way the date holds

decisions.decision: status.json is the source of truth, status.md is generated from it
decisions.rationale: Machine-readable state for tooling, readable view for humans, no divergence
Chosen by the project owner; shortest and most permissive, maximises adoption

decisions.decision: Project renamed to PackForge4UEM before any code was written
decisions.rationale: Drops the word 'Manager', which collided with App Volumes Manager, an actual Omnissa server component, and removes the leading hyphen that command line tools parse as an option flag. Free to do while the repository is empty, expensive after publication

openQuestions.question: Is a Workspace ONE UEM tenant with API access available for live verification?
openQuestions.impact: Blocks schema verification for blob upload, internal application creation and Freestyle workflow import. Drives the E04 approach
openQuestions.assumedAnswer: Not available - proceeding mock-first against documentation

openQuestions.question: Is a second UEM tenant available, so multi-tenant fan-out can be tested for real rather than simulated?
Is an App Volumes Manager instance with API access available?
GitHub organisation and final repository URL
Trademark review of the name - 'App Volumes Manager' is the name of an actual Omnissa server component, so PackForge4UEM may read as an official module
openQuestions.impact: Naming risk before publication to Omnissa Community
openQuestions.answer: Renamed to PackForge4UEM; the colliding word is gone

openQuestions.question: The repository name begins with a hyphen ('-PackForge4UEM'), which many command line tools parse as an option flag. Rename, or keep and document the workaround?
openQuestions.impact: Affects clone instructions, CI configuration and scripts referencing the repository
openQuestions.answer: Leading hyphen removed by the rename

risks.risk: The Freestyle Orchestrator workflow JSON schema and its import API surface are unverified. Historically Freestyle exposed less through the API than through the console
risks.mitigation: Mock-first development behind an interface; verify against a live tenant as soon as one exists; treat the generator as replaceable

risks.risk: Four weeks to the deadline for three components and two external integrations
risks.mitigation: Narrow MVP (D14), OpenAPI contract frozen in W1 to unblock parallel work, launch content treated as a deliverable rather than an afterthought
WAL mode plus serialised writes designed in from the start (D04); load test the fan-out path in W3

risks.risk: Large artifact uploads from the agent failing mid-transfer
risks.mitigation: Chunked resumable upload with hash verification; a dropped connection must not discard a completed build

risks.risk: Credentials for multiple UEM tenants concentrated in one service
risks.mitigation: Secrets encrypted at rest, never returned through the API, audit log on every use; mTLS for agents (D07)

risks.risk: Trademark confusion from the project name and from referencing Omnissa product names
risks.mitigation: Explicit non-affiliation disclaimer in the README; resolve Q06 before publication
